extraction.name: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
extraction.description: Labeled subsets of the tiny images dataset: CIFAR-10 has ten object classes with 6000 images each, and CIFAR-100 has 600 images in each of 100 classes.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Students were paid to label a subset of the tiny images dataset by filtering noisy web-search labels; labelers examined images found with a class search term and its WordNet hyponyms, rejected images not belonging to the assigned class, duplicates were removed, and the data was split into training and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source was the tiny images dataset collected from web image search results for every non-abstract English noun in WordNet, using search engines including Google, Flickr, and AltaVista.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Perfect duplicates and overly white images were removed from the tiny images source; for CIFAR labeling, duplicate images were removed using L2 norm thresholding; the dataset was split into training and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Paid student labelers were assigned a class and asked to examine images retrieved with that class term and its WordNet hyponyms, rejecting images that did not belong to the class according to specified criteria such as likely category name, photo-realism, single prominent instance, and clear identity under occlusion or unusual viewpoint; every submitted label was personally verified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Every label submitted by the labelers was personally verified.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The original tiny images labels are extremely unreliable because they come from web search terms.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The original tiny images dataset has no reliable class labels, making it hard to use for object recognition experiments.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: CIFAR-10 was used for object classification experiments with training and test splits; CIFAR-100 can be used as negative examples for CIFAR-10.
